problem: Post-merge CodeQL could remain running while all borging/skill-projection checks were green, and agents could hand that pending status back to the user.
root_cause: The Python CodeQL workflow used github.run_id for push-event concurrency, so newer main pushes could not supersede stale same-ref work. Separately, terminal-delivery guidance did not explicitly forbid handing back an active authoritative post-merge security run.
fix: Use stable CodeQL concurrency keyed by workflow plus PR number/ref with cancel-in-progress=true; retain the existing stable Powerhouse CodeQL same-ref policy; make the newest exact-SHA run authoritative; forbid final user handoff while that authoritative security run is active.
prevention: Use stable PR/ref identity for CodeQL concurrency; never github.run_id.
Treat only the newest relevant exact-SHA security run as authoritative.
Do not return queued/running post-merge security state as a final user handoff.
Record NOT_APPLICABLE only from explicit path-filter evidence.
evidence: .github/workflows/codeql.yml previously used github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id while cancel-in-progress was true.
.github/workflows/powerhouse-codeql.yml already uses stable PR/ref latest-wins concurrency and remains the reference pattern.
